hypothesis: In the MODBUS_FC_WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS handler, the address check tests 'mapping_address < 0' twice and never tests 'mapping_address_write < 0'. An attacker can send a write address (address_write) lower than mb_mapping->start_registers, for example when the mapping starts at a non-zero address. mapping_address_write then becomes negative, and the write loop at lines 978-982 stores attacker-controlled values at mb_mapping->tab_registers[negative index]. This is a heap buffer underflow (out-of-bounds write).
evidence_source: Line 953 computes 'int mapping_address_write = address_write - mb_mapping->start_registers;'. The check at lines 962-965 reads 'mapping_address < 0 || (mapping_address + nb) > nb_registers || mapping_address < 0 || (mapping_address_write + nb_write) > nb_registers'; the second 'mapping_address < 0' should be 'mapping_address_write < 0'. The loop at lines 978-981 then executes 'mb_mapping->tab_registers[i] = ...' with i starting at mapping_address_write.
input_artifact: not_available (static source review; no input artifact)
expected_behavior: Set up a server whose mapping has start_registers > 0. Send FC 0x17 with a valid read address and a write address below start_registers. ASan should report a heap-buffer-overflow (write before the tab_registers allocation), or the heap is silently corrupted.
observed_behavior: not_available (static source review; nothing was executed)
notes: This matches CVE-2022-0367. The upper-bound check alone does not catch the case: a negative mapping_address_write plus a small nb_write stays at or below nb_registers. With start_registers == 0, address_write is a uint16_t, so the index cannot go negative; the defect requires a shifted mapping.
